author_review.both: Single advisory cycle completed. Invalid-control gating already existed in each first draft; advice did not remove it. No semantic publication gate was added.

accepted_decision.explanation: Identity mapping shows session-red maps to account A and session-blue maps to account B per obs-1. Permission policy per obs-2 grants A access to A and B access to B only. Own-account requests: session-red/A (obs-3) and session-blue/B (obs-5) both returned status 200 with body error "not authorized" despite policy allowing access. Cross-account requests: session-red/B (obs-4) and session-blue/A (obs-6) returned error not authorized, matching denial expectation but own-account denials contradict policy. Therefore access outcomes do not align with policy, classification is violation.

cases.explanation_review: Error labels are treated as denial despite returned protected data; correct label with incorrect reasoning
recommendations: Header-selector authorization comparison with policy, identity and invalid-value controls

accepted_decision.explanation: Identity bindings: session-red→A, session-blue→B per obs-1. Policy: A permissions [A,B], B permissions [B] per obs-2. Own-account reads: session-red/A returns object owner A value record-A obs-3; session-blue/B returns object owner B value record-B obs-5. Cross-account reads: session-red/B returns object owner B value record-B obs-4, which is permitted by policy A→B; session-blue/A returns no object, error not authorized obs-6, which matches policy denial B→A. Access outcomes align with observed permission policy; no unauthorized disclosure observed in tested pairs.

feedback.reason: The observed task behavior demonstrates concrete application of the delivered header-selector authorization comparison methodology. Identity and policy are recorded, authentication is held constant while the selector is varied, and protected object data attributable to the policy-denied selector is observed in the response content despite an error label, which is the discriminating comparison the guidance describes. The evidence mappings link the guidance controls and verification steps to the specific observations and published classification.

accepted_decision.explanation: Identity bindings: session-red→A, session-blue→B (obs-1). Policy: A permissions [A,B], B permissions [B] (obs-2). Own-account and cross-account checks all returned status 200 with error not authorized. Object presence indicates effective access: session-red (A) accessed A (obs-3) and B (obs-4); session-blue (B) accessed B (obs-5) but not A (obs-6, no object). Effective access matches policy: A can read A,B; B can read B only. No unauthorized cross-account access observed.
